# Task: every new note is refused

Since the last release, every `POST /notes` from the mobile app is answered
`400 Bad Request`. The app has not changed: it sends what `API.md` says, for
example `{"text":"buy milk"}` with `Content-Type: application/json` and a
valid token. Reading notes still works.

Find out why and fix it.
# Notes API

The contract the notes service keeps with its clients. Every answer below is
relied on by a client; a change to one is a change to this document first.

## Every route

- A request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the scheme is matched
  in any case (`bearer` too). The service reads its tokens at start-up, one
  `token user` pair per line of its tokens file.
- A missing, malformed or unknown token: `401`, body `Unauthorized`, and the
  field `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
- A note is visible to its owner only: anyone else gets the same `404` as for
  a note that does not exist.
- JSON is sent and received as `Content-Type: application/json`. A note is
  `{"id":1,"owner":"ada","text":"buy milk"}`, its members in that order.
- A request the service cannot read (a path value that is not a number, a
  JSON body that is malformed or lacks a member) is `400`, body
  `Bad Request`, with its cause written to the service's standard error.

## Routes

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /notes` | `200`, the caller's notes, oldest first: `[{"id":1,...}]`, or `[]` |
| `GET /notes/{id}` | `200`, the note; `404`, body `no note {id}`, when there is none the caller owns |
| `POST /notes`, body `{"text":"..."}` | `201`, the note as stored, with its new id; `422`, body `text too long`, when the text is longer than the service's limit in bytes |

## Storage

Notes are kept in a journal file and read back at start-up. A note whose write
fails is not kept: the client gets `503`, body `storage unavailable`, the
cause is written to standard error, and the next write succeeds once the
journal can be written again. The next note takes the id the failed one did
not use.

## Running the service

    PROGRAM PORT JOURNAL TOKENS MAX_TEXT

`MAX_TEXT` is the longest text accepted, in bytes.
#!/bin/sh
# Builds ./notes from notes_flare.mojo.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec /root/.pixi/bin/pixi run --manifest-path /home/user/muntin/pixi.toml --frozen -e flare mojo build -I . notes_flare.mojo -o notes
#!/bin/sh
# Serves ./notes on 127.0.0.1:PORT (default 8080), its journal in
# journal.log, its tokens in tokens (t-ada is ada, t-bo is bo), texts
# up to 40 bytes.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec ./notes "${1:-8080}" journal.log tokens 40

input.message:
Every `POST /notes` failed because of a field name in the web layer. The body type `NewNote` in `notes_flare.mojo` called its only field `content`, but the client sends `{"text":"..."}`, as `API.md` says. The JSON decoder (`deserialize_value`) matches JSON members to struct fields by name, so every correct request was missing a `content` member and got `400 Bad Request`. The service's standard error showed the cause: `[flare:bad-request] rid=- missing required field 'content' for notes_flare.NewNote`. Reading notes never uses this type, which is why reads still worked.

**Fix:** I renamed the field to `text`, updated the one place that reads it in `CreateNote.serve`, and added a comment saying the field name must match the JSON member. `./build.sh` succeeds.

**Checked against the running server:**
- `{"text":"buy milk"}` with `Bearer` or lowercase `bearer` gets `201` and the note in the documented member order. Ids go up from 1.
- A 40-byte text is accepted; a 41-byte text gets `422 text too long`.
- `{"content":...}`, malformed JSON and `/notes/abc` all get `400 Bad Request`, with the cause written to standard error.
- A missing or unknown token gets `401 Unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
- Another user's note gets `404 no note 2`, and `GET /notes` returns only the caller's notes, oldest first.
- After a restart the journal is read back and the next id continues from it.

I did not test the `503 storage unavailable` path.

**Files changed:** only `/srv/runs/r24/notes_flare.mojo`. `API.md` needed no change: the code had drifted from the contract, not the other way round. Besides that, only the rebuilt `./notes` binary differs. The server I started on port 20240 has been stopped, and I removed my temporary files (`journal.log`, pid and log files).

**Unsure of:** I couldn't read the JSON library's source, because it is installed outside the run directory. So "matches members by field name" comes from its error message and how it behaved, not from its documentation.
